## Chosen hook

Line 1 (Contrarian, aimed at the metric men are counting, never at the GP who suggested it):

"Most men who are tired all the time are counting the wrong number."

Re-hook: "They count hours in bed. Hours in bed is not the number that decides how you feel."

## Script

**Funnel:** TOFU (Attract) | job: problem-aware scroll-stop (sleep quality vs tiredness) | cta: canonical-article | format: linkedin-post | marker: none
**Emotion:** Recognition, with vindication underneath. He followed the advice. It was not his failure that it did not work.
**Source:** `why-am-i-always-tired` (Pillar B hub, published 2026-06-19, Ewa-signed).

POST

> Most men who are tired all the time are counting the wrong number.
>
> They count hours in bed. Eight hours in bed can be six hours of broken, shallow sleep, and on paper the eight still looks fine.
>
> A nightcap. A scroll in the dark. A bedroom that is slightly too warm. A weekend lie-in that shifts your body clock two hours out and back again by Monday. None of those change the number you are counting. All of them change how you feel at two in the afternoon.
>
> The NHS guidance here is unglamorous: six to nine hours, and keep your sleep and wake times roughly the same. The consistency is doing more work than the total.
>
> So "get more sleep" can be sound advice and still be useless.
>
> There is also a difference between being sleepy and being tired all the time, and almost nobody gets told it. Sleepy is a signal you can fix tonight. The flat kind, where the coffee works for an hour and then the floor comes back up to meet you, is rarely one bad night. It is an accumulation.
>
> And it is usually not one big thing. It is five small things you stopped noticing: sleep quality, a stress load that never switches off, training that has outrun recovery, alcohol, and what you eat at breakfast.
>
> Which gives you a test rather than a theory. Change two or three of them and hold it for a fortnight. A single tired week tells you nothing. A fortnight of honest changes tells you whether the cause is on that list.
>
> If your energy moves, you had your answer and it cost you nothing.
>
> If it does not move, that is the useful result. That is the point where measuring earns its place, instead of being one more thing you buy on a hunch. That is the moment Andro Prime is built for.
>
> When someone last told you to get more sleep, did you ever find out whether it was the sleep?

**First comment:** I am building Andro Prime, plain-English men's health read from your blood. The full version, including the five causes, what to change this week, and the point where this stops being a lifestyle question and becomes a GP one, is here: https://andro-prime.com/blog/why-am-i-always-tired?utm_source=linkedin

## Craft notes

- **Structure chosen on avatar fit, and that is the axis it was ranked on.** Two angles were viable from this hub. The first is the five-causes listicle, whose implicit ask is "go away and audit five inputs", which is more unassessed reading and therefore aimed straight at Mark's actual problem rather than at his question (`avatar-mark.md` §A, "read enough to be dangerous and not enough to be sure"). The second, chosen, asks him to reinterpret advice he has already been given and already followed, which he can do in a single pass while reading. Both sit on the same proof rung (`hook-rubric.md` §4), since neither carries a first-hand result, so the tie broke on avatar fit alone. Compliance ease played no part: both clear.
- **Archetype:** Contrarian, the LinkedIn default. The wedge is pointed at the metric men count, not at the person who suggested it. "Get more sleep" is called sound and useless in the same sentence, which keeps the energy on the measurement and off the profession, the line `hook-playbook.md` §2 draws around this archetype.
- **Device 7, understatement at the peak:** "So 'get more sleep' can be sound advice and still be useless." Shortest paragraph in the post, carrying the turn.
- **Device 6, the banal scene carries the load:** the nightcap, the scroll in the dark, the too-warm bedroom, two in the afternoon, the floor coming back up to meet you. All five are the article's own details, not invented texture.
- **No personal history and no bloodwork figure.** The only first-person claims are a statement about the business and a statement of intent, the same discipline as `looking-for-a-word`. Nothing here is written as Mark.
- **Distance from the other assets off this hub.** `four-worth-seeing` (published 2026-07-28) ran the what-was-measured wedge off a result you already have. `the-stack` and `when-a-test-earns-its-place` are the short-form pair. This post starts before any test exists, from advice rather than from paper, and its subject is the input rather than the marker. It can run alongside them without repeating any of them.
- **`marker: none` is deliberate.** The post does not lead on a biomarker; the one measurement line names the Kit 2 trio collectively through the hub rather than promoting a single marker. Every marker the hub then names (Vitamin D, Active B12, ferritin, hs-CRP) is in a live kit, so the hook-playbook §4 live-marker rail holds.

## Rails held

Written as an allowlist of what the copy does, never a list of what it avoids, because a note spelling out the red-flag terms puts them back into the scanned file (Observation 83).

The post stays on the education side throughout. It describes what a common metric does and does not capture, quotes the NHS sleep guidance through the hub, and names five possible contributors to one feeling without attributing it to any of them. Its contrarian energy is aimed at the number men count. It names no ingredient and no product, so the EFSA tables are not in play. It carries no personal result and no figure beyond the NHS hours range quoted from the hub. The founder is disclosed in the body, which the LinkedIn format expects. What is offered is a way to tell which cause is yours, framed as measurement and never as an outcome. The single CTA is a soft link in the first comment routed to the canonical hub, which carries the kit routing and the GP-referral wording onward, so nothing here points at a kit or at the founding-member list. Full `https://` scheme on the link per Keith's 2026-07-31 rule. No em dashes, no bullet lists in the post body, no engagement bait.
